headline.headline: MANZARDO WALK-OFF BLAST SILENCES PHILLY IN THE NINTH
headline.deck: Cleveland first baseman's fifth homer delivers Guardians a 1-0 stunner at Philadelphia
headline.body:
PHILADELPHIA — Kyle Manzardo stepped to the plate as a pinch hitter in the top of the ninth inning Friday night at Citizens Bank Park and did something no one else could manage in eight innings of deadlock: he put a ball over the fence. Manzardo's solo home run, his fifth of the season, was the only run of the night in a 1-0 Cleveland Guardians victory over the Philadelphia Phillies before a crowd of 38,092 that went home in stunned silence.

The game was a masterpiece of scoreless baseball through the first eight frames, with neither starter yielding a run. Then Manzardo, pinch-hitting for Rhys Hoskins, turned on a pitch and drove it out to give Cleveland its margin of victory and push the Guardians to 31-22, firmly atop the AL Central. The Phillies, losers of three straight, fell to 25-26 and slipped further from the NL East lead.

For Philadelphia, the loss was a continuation of a troubling stretch. The Phillies managed to strand runners and squander chances against a Cleveland pitching staff that was stingy from the first pitch to the last. The game was completed in a crisp 2 hours and 5 minutes, leaving Phillies fans with little to cheer and much to ponder heading into the weekend.

secondary.headline: WEMBANYAMA VOWS TO PLAY FOR TEAM AFTER THUNDER TAKE 2-1 LEAD
secondary.deck: Spurs star scores 26 but calls for more collective effort after 123-108 Game 3 defeat
secondary.body:
SAN ANTONIO — Victor Wembanyama poured in a team-high 26 points Friday night, but it was not nearly enough as the Oklahoma City Thunder pulled away for a 123-108 victory over the San Antonio Spurs, seizing a 2-1 lead in the Western Conference semifinals. The Thunder, who finished the regular season 64-18, showed why they are the class of the West, exploiting San Antonio's defensive breakdowns in a dominant performance.

Wembanyama, the Spurs' cornerstone and the focal point of San Antonio's long-term ambitions, was candid after the game. He acknowledged that individual brilliance was insufficient and said he needed to be more of a team player going forward. With Game 4 on the horizon, the Spurs face the urgent task of evening the series before returning to Oklahoma City. San Antonio finished the regular season 62-20, so talent is not the issue — cohesion and execution are.

secondary.headline: GOLDEN KNIGHTS HOLD 2-0 SERIES EDGE OVER AVALANCHE HEADING WEST
secondary.deck: Vegas escapes Denver with back-to-back wins; Colorado laments squandered early leads
secondary.body:
DENVER — The Vegas Golden Knights defeated the Colorado Avalanche 3-1 in Game 2 of the Western Conference finals, taking a commanding 2-0 series lead back to T-Mobile Arena. Colorado coach Jared Bednar was visibly frustrated after the game, noting that his team had real chances to extend a 1-0 lead before the Knights turned the game on its head and closed it out.

Jack Eichel and Nicolas Barbashev were central to the Vegas surge that broke open a tight contest. The Avalanche, who finished the regular season at 55-16-11, entered the playoffs as legitimate Cup contenders, but they have now dropped two straight to a Golden Knights squad built for this moment. Colorado must regroup and find answers before the series shifts to Nevada, where Vegas has been nearly unbeatable in playoff hockey.

secondary.headline: RAYS ERUPT FOR FOUR IN EIGHTH TO DOWN YANKEES, STAY HOT AT 34-15
secondary.deck: Tampa Bay's stunning eighth-inning rally sinks New York 4-2 in the Bronx
secondary.body:
NEW YORK — The Tampa Bay Rays entered the eighth inning at Yankee Stadium trailing 2-0 Friday night, then proceeded to score four times in a single frame to stun the home crowd of 41,358 and walk away with a 4-2 victory. The win extended Tampa Bay's torrid run and kept the Rays at 34-15, the best record in the AL East and one of the best in all of baseball. Jonathan Aranda and Mullin each doubled in the inburst that broke the game open.

Patrick Wells had hit a home run, his fourth of the year, to give the Yankees a 1-0 lead in the fifth, and New York added another run in the eighth before Tampa Bay's rally made it academic. The Yankees, at 30-22, remain second in the AL East but find themselves chasing a Rays team that shows no signs of slowing down. The two clubs meet again Saturday, with Tampa Bay riding momentum and New York searching for answers against its division rival.

column.headline: WEMBANYAMA IS BRILLIANT, BUT BRILLIANCE ALONE WON'T BEAT OKLAHOMA CITY
column.body:
Victor Wembanyama is already one of the most captivating players in the NBA, and on Friday night in San Antonio he delivered 26 points against the most dangerous team in the Western Conference. It was not enough. The Thunder won by 15, and the Spurs now face a must-win situation in Game 4 on their own floor. Wembanyama's admission that he must be more of a team player was refreshing, but the real question is whether San Antonio's supporting cast can actually answer the call when it matters most.

Oklahoma City finished 64-18 for a reason. They are deep, disciplined, and relentlessly well-coached, and they do not allow individual performances to beat them. If Wembanyama wants to drag San Antonio past this Thunder squad, he will need shooters hitting open looks, bigs setting productive screens, and a bench that does not disappear in critical stretches. The talent gap between these two franchises is razor thin on paper. But the Thunder play like a unit, and until the Spurs match that cohesion, Wembanyama's brilliance will keep producing narrow moral victories that do nothing for the series column.

story.headline: BRAVES WALK OFF NATIONALS IN 11 TO SNAP EXTRA-INNING THRILLER
story.deck: Atlanta survives Washington rally in tenth to win wild five-hour battle
story.body:
ATLANTA — The Braves needed 11 innings and every last out they could muster, but Atlanta walked off the Washington Nationals 5-4 Friday night at Truist Park in the most dramatic finish on the major league slate. Washington forced extra innings by scoring twice in the tenth to tie the game at four, only to watch Atlanta answer with the deciding run in the bottom of the eleventh to end a 3:13 grind before 36,082 fans.

The game turned on a pair of power strokes. Jackson Mead clubbed his fifth home run of the season for Atlanta, while Washington's CJ Abrams provided a jolt of his own with his 11th blast, a triple to go along with it, and stolen base as part of a relentless Nationals attack that kept Atlanta from putting the game away through nine regulation innings. The Braves scored two in the seventh to briefly take control, but Washington clawed back with a run in the eighth and two more in the tenth.

Elsewhere around the majors, the Tampa Bay Rays continued their torrid pace by stunning the New York Yankees 4-2 in the Bronx, scoring all four of their runs in a stunning eighth-inning eruption to improve to 34-15 atop the AL East. Kyle Manzardo delivered a walk-off solo home run in the ninth inning — his fifth of the year — as the Cleveland Guardians edged the Philadelphia Phillies 1-0, and Byron Buxton crushed his 16th homer to power the Minnesota Twins past the Boston Red Sox 8-6 in a back-and-forth slugfest at Fenway Park.

story.headline: THUNDER STORM BACK FROM 15 DOWN TO SEIZE 2-1 SERIES LEAD OVER SPURS
story.deck: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander leads Oklahoma City's stunning rally in San Antonio
story.body:
SAN ANTONIO — Oklahoma City Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and his teammates authored one of the more dramatic reversals of this postseason Friday night, erasing a 15-point deficit to beat the San Antonio Spurs 123-108 at the AT&T Center and grab a 2-1 advantage in their Western Conference semifinal series.

Victor Wembanyama led all scorers with 26 points for San Antonio, but the Spurs' young franchise centerpiece admitted afterward the performance was not enough. "Got to be more of a team player," Wembanyama said, a candid acknowledgment that Oklahoma City's collective depth overwhelmed San Antonio's reliance on its 22-year-old phenom. The Thunder, who finished the regular season 64-18 and owned the West's top seed, demonstrated precisely why that record was earned, grinding through adversity on the road before pulling away decisively.

Gilgeous-Alexander addressed Spurs fans' chants directed at him following the final buzzer, brushing off the crowd noise with the composure of a player who has carried Oklahoma City all season. The Thunder now return to San Antonio for Game 4 holding command of a series that features two of the Western Conference's most formidable rosters, with the second-seeded Spurs at 62-20 facing an urgent need to even things before the series shifts back to Oklahoma City.

story.headline: EICHEL, BARBASHEV STUN AVALANCHE AS KNIGHTS SEIZE 2-0 SERIES EDGE
story.deck: Vegas scores twice in 2:07 of the third period to erase Colorado's lead
story.body:
LAS VEGAS — Jack Eichel and Ivan Barbashev struck 2:07 apart in the third period Friday night, turning a one-goal deficit into a 3-1 victory and handing the Vegas Golden Knights a commanding 2-0 series lead over the Colorado Avalanche in the Western Conference finals. The Avalanche, who carried a 1-0 advantage into the final frame, watched their lead evaporate in a burst that left Ball Arena hushed and the Knights celebrating their second straight road triumph.

Colorado coach Jared Bednar acknowledged after the game that his club had opportunities to push the margin beyond a single goal before the third period arrived, chances that ultimately proved costly. The Avalanche, the Central Division's dominant force at 55-16-11 this season, now face the uncomfortable reality of heading back to Denver down two games against a Vegas squad that finished the regular year at 39-26-17 but has raised its play dramatically in the postseason.

Game 3 shifts to Colorado, where the Avalanche will need to respond or risk falling into a 3-0 hole. Vegas has shown the ability to win ugly and win late, a combination that has Colorado's celebrated roster searching for answers before the series reaches a potentially decisive stretch.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILDLY AS TEAMS RETOOL FOR 2026 CAMPAIGN
story.deck: Three franchises swap signal-callers in a week as the offseason market heats up.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has erupted into a frenzy of quarterback movement, with at least three franchises reshuffling their depth charts in a span of seven days. The Las Vegas Raiders completed a blockbuster trade sending veteran starter Gardner Minshew to the Carolina Panthers in exchange for a package of draft picks, while the New Orleans Saints inked free agent Sam Darnold to a two-year deal worth $54 million, banking on his resurgent 2025 campaign to stabilize a offense that ranked 28th in scoring last season.

The draft class from last month's event in Green Bay continues to generate debate among front offices and analysts alike. Colorado wide receiver and consensus first-round talent Javon McKinley landed with the New England Patriots at pick seven, and early reports out of Foxborough suggest offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels has already installed a package of jet sweeps and quick slants designed specifically around the 6-foot-2 speedster. Meanwhile, the Dallas Cowboys drew scrutiny for selecting an interior offensive lineman in the first round rather than addressing their glaring need at cornerback, a decision head coach Brian Schottenheimer defended at the team's post-draft press conference.

Training camp storylines are already taking shape across the league. In Pittsburgh, second-year linebacker Damarius Cole is pushing for a starting role after an impressive spring minicamp, while the defending Super Bowl LX champion Kansas City Chiefs face questions about whether aging pass rusher Chris Jones has enough left in the tank following offseason knee surgery. Jones, 31, told reporters last week he expects to be full-go by late July when padded practices begin, though the Chiefs have quietly explored depth options along the defensive line just in case.
